chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abdul-Hamid, from Al-Sabah, the servant of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when we passed by Uhud. He said: Do you see the hole in it? I said: Yes. He said: As for me, I do not see it. And the signs of old age are three: dullness of sight, bending of the back, and thinning of the feet.

key_terms.أُحُد: Mount Uhud, a prominent mountain near Medina

ai.seo_question: What are the three physical signs of old age according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) demonstrates the relativity of sensory perception by contrasting his companion’s clear vision of a hole in Mount Uhud with his own diminished sight, attributing this not to pathology but to the natural process of aging. He codifies this observation into three distinct physical markers of old age: weakened vision (*kalal al-basar*), a stooped posture (*inhiya’ al-zahr*), and thinning of the feet (*warq al-qadam*), reflecting the gradual decline of bodily faculties. This narration serves as a practical guide for understanding the physiological signs of aging within the Shia tradition, emphasizing acceptance of these changes as part of the divine decree.
